main_text.p: sub Anastasio imperatore, & postea sub Heraclio viguit, imprimisque a Syris Monachis defensa est, & saepe sub disputationis de duabus in Christo naturis praetextu interpolata, & velut crambe bis.cocta iterum appositā. Denique novo Christolytarum nomine, quorum meminit Dam-mascenus, repetita. Ephesina Synodo prima, cui praefuit Cyrillus Alexandriae episcopus, sub Theodosio iuniore, confutatus est hic error: deinde a Zenone imperatore, tota Edessae civi-tatis schola, quod Nestorianum dogma probaret, euersa est, vt Theodoretus libro 2. scribit. Denique legibus etiam publicis & Romanis, punita & coercita, vt apparet ex l. Damnato. C. De haeretic. & Manich. & meminit etiam illius legis Euagr. libro 1. capite 12. & post eum Nicephorus libro 14. vt nihil isto dogmate tetrius, putidius, & odiosius vniuersis Ecclesiis, totiqué terrarum orbi vnquam fuerit. Quis autem huius sectae & haereseos primus author fuerit, vel censendus sit, quaesitum iampridem legimus. Quidam enim a Photinianis haereticis velut propaginem quandam deducunt: alij a Samosatenianis, vel Paulianis potius ortam malunt, quemadmodum Suidas in voce Nestorius. quorum omnium sententiam refutat Socrates libro 7. cap. 32. Verisimilius diceretur a Manichaeis professa, qui, vt scribit Augustinus libro 23. contra Faustum, docent alium esse in Christo Filium Dei, alium autem Filium Mariae (non tantum autem aliud) & Filium Dei in Baptismo Christi descendisse in Filium Mariae. page.notes: Reading is partly uncertain at several points due to the scan: "Dam-mascenus" is printed "Damascenus" (hyphenated at line end, lightly printed); the word after "in Christo" and several Greek words (Nestorius, Suidas entry) are faint. Lines near the bottom are slightly smudged; the final word "quod &" is cut off at the lower edge. Some words ("appositā", "sub", "Nicephorus", "Edessae") are marked as uncertain where the scan is faint; the Greek in the Suidas reference was read as NESTORIUS and should be checked. Page marked by the printed head "DE HAERESIBVS." and number 224. No catchword or signature visible.
